author: Jacob Sussman
about: Machine-readable index of the result of this repository: explicit circuits for the Walsh-Hadamard transform with fewer operations than the textbook program. It is a better constant in front of N log2 N, not a better exponent. The account in words is in explicit-circuits.md, in this folder.

counts.G: one operation is one a*u + b*v with any constants a, b; multiplying by a constant is free
counts.O: every addition, every subtraction and every multiplication by a constant costs one; the gate set of OpenAI's circuit model (lean/OAI/Computability/FourierCircuit/Core.lean)
counts.textbook: N log2 N in both counts
counts.G_and_the_1994_paper: Coppersmith, Feig and Linzer (1994, page 969) charge one for a multiply-add, +-a +- b*c, for a plain addition and for a plain multiplication. Count G is wider, because it allows a constant on both terms. No circuit here uses that: every line has at most one constant (tools/circuits/multiply_add_check.py), so each count G below is also the circuit's count in the sense of the 1994 paper

status_values.lean: a theorem in lean/Work/SmallWHT/ of this repository, accepted by Lean 4.34.1 on one Linux machine in a build of the folder lean/ from nothing with lake; lean/tools/Compare.lean passed; the official comparator was not run on this folder
status_values.python: replayed exactly by the Python programs of tools/circuits/ on every unit input; not checked in Lean
status_values.on_paper: argued in writing by the AI agents of this project; not in Lean, without a human review

how_to_read.new: 'not found in print' means: not found in the literature search described in explicit-circuits.md, section 7; it is not a proof of novelty
how_to_read.review: The reports behind this index were written by AI agents (Anthropic's Claude) that I directed, on 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11. They have not had a line-by-line human review. The additions of revision 2 (2026-10-22) were made the same way: by AI agents that I directed, without a line-by-line human review.

not_a_change_of_order: Every count here is a fixed fraction of N log2 N. Results that lower the exponent, such as OpenAI's result of 2026-09-25 for the Fourier transform, are of a smaller order: below every fixed fraction of N log2 N for large N. Those results give nothing at any size anyone computes. Revision 2: in the same circuit model, OpenAI's family 130 proves circuits below c n log2 n for every c > 0 for the Fourier transform at some very large lengths; for this transform, wht-power-saving-lean proves in Lean an order N (log2 N)^z with z = 1 - 1.57e-3 in OpenAI's model of a computer with memory (see literature.asymptotic_results).

lean.statement_in_words: for every j, the exact Walsh-Hadamard transform on N = 8^j points has a circuit in OpenAI's circuit model with at most 20*j*8^(j-1) + 8^j gates, which is (5/6) N log2 N + N
lean.theorem_text: theorem hadamard_pow8_circuit (j : Nat) : exists C : Circuit (2 ^ (3 * j)), C.Computes (hadamard (3 * j)) /\ C.size <= 20 * (j * 8 ^ (j - 1)) + 8 ^ j

not_claimed: running time: the 8-point step was written into the generated code of the library FFHT in place of its 24-operation block and timed on one machine on 2026-10-11; it was not faster at any size from 2^6 to 2^26 points (from 2^5 in double precision), in any of three forms (tools/circuits/fast/wht56/results/ffht/README.md); in my own plain C on two machines the time did not follow the operation count (tools/circuits/fast/wht56/results/bench-by-size/bench.md)

hardware: as one block of adders with no registers inside, the 19-adder 8-point circuit takes 274 logic cells against 349 for the textbook network on a Lattice iCE40HX8K (273 against 337 with the synthesis option -dff); it is twice as deep, slower by the tools' estimates, larger than the textbook when pipelined, and not the smallest design on that chip; no existing design was improved (tools/circuits/fpga/README.md)

optimality: at 8 points the minimum in count G is between 15 and 19; the lower bound 2N - 1 (15 at 8 points) is Proposition 6 of the paper in paper/, with a proof written by the AI agents on 2026-10-11 and read by a second agent and by no person, not in Lean; 19 is the exact minimum only among circuits of its own shape, by two exhaustive searches (python)
novelty beyond the literature search described in explicit-circuits.md
an asymptotic record: counts of a smaller order are known (literature.asymptotic_results); this is an explicit constant at practical sizes

running time, revision 2: a few percent less time at best, on AMD Zen 4 and Zen 5, against the best textbook code in the same program; no gain on AMD Zen 2 or on a GPU; slower on an Intel Broadwell; no gain at 64 to 512 points on Zen 4; one run per chip; see measurements_2026_10_22
the same output as FFHT bit for bit on real data: the rounding differs (measurements_2026_10_22, F13)
that the kernel in tools/fht-kernel/ is fast as a library: it has not been timed on its own
a smaller FPGA design on every chip: a loss on a Xilinx Artix-7 (measurements_2026_10_22, F16); power not measured
peer review: the paper was not reviewed and not submitted

stated_count_of_grigoryan_and_agaian_200.stated: 6*2^r - r^2 - 3r - 6 additions and subtractions for N = 2^r points (page 181)
stated_count_of_grigoryan_and_agaian_200.finding: the stated count is too small: the recursion that the algorithm follows, T(N) = (2N - 2) + T(N/2) + ... + T(1), T(1) = 0, gives exactly N log2 N
stated_count_of_grigoryan_and_agaian_200.bound: (N/2) log2 N is a lower bound for circuits of additions and subtractions, by the determinant argument of Morgenstern (1973) as Alman and Rao quote it; the introduction of the paper gives 0.5 N log N as a lower bound for the Hadamard transform (page 172)
